text: EX-10.1 2 ea031309301ex10-1.htm EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 20, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN DAVID CAPLON AND QUANTUM CYBER N.V Exhibit 10.1 EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT This Agreement (the “ Agreement ”), is made and entered into as of November 20, 2026 (the “ Agreement Date ”), by and between Quantum Cyber N.V. (the “ Company ”), and David Caplon (the “ CFO ”, and together with the Company, the “ Parties ”) NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth below, it is hereby covenanted and agreed by the Company and the CFO as follows: 1. Employment. Effective November 20, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), the Company hereby agrees to employ the CFO to the Company in the position of Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”) and the CFO, in such capacity, agrees to the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth. The CFO shall have the customary powers, responsibilities, and authorities of a chief financial officer of corporations of the size, type and nature of the Company, as it exists from time to time. The CFO shall report directly to the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and shall have direct access to the Board and its Audit Committee. CFO’s principal work location shall be CFO’s home office or such other remote location as approved by the Company. The parties acknowledge and agree that the position is a remote role. CFO may be required to travel periodically for meetings, conferences, Board presentations, audits, investor relations activities, acquisitions, or other business purposes as reasonably requested by the Company. Any material change requiring CFO to relocate or regularly report to a Company office shall constitute a material adverse change in CFO’s working conditions and may provide a basis for Good Reason under Section 4(b)(ii). The Company acknowledges that the CFO currently provides services to other companies and agrees that the CFO may continue such activities, provided that they do not materially interfere with the performance of his duties hereunder or create a conflict of interest with the Company. 2. Compensation . During the Term, the Company shall provide the following compensation to the CFO for his services hereunder: (a) Salary . The Company shall pay CFO a base salary of $22,500 per month ($270,000 on an annualized basis), less applicable taxes and withholdings, in accordance with the Company’s standard payroll procedures (the “ Base Salary ”). The Company shall review the Base Salary at least annually for merit, performance, and market competitiveness, and the Base Salary may be increased during the Term, taking into consideration the CFO’s performance, responsibilities, and prevailing market compensation for similarly situated executive officers. (b) Annual Incentive Awards . During the Term, CFO shall be eligible to receive annual grants in the form of (i) options, (ii) restricted stock or restricted stock units, (iii) stock grants, or (iv) such other equity-based awards as the Company may determine in its discretion (collectively, the “ Awards ”), with the value of such Awards at the time of grant equivalent to up to the greater of (x) the value of 250,000 ordinary shares and (y) 100% of the annual Base Salary. Such awards shall be subject to the Company’s 2025 Omnibus Incentive Plan, as amended (the “ Plan ”) and shall be subject to the Compensation Committee of the Board, and shall have no less favorable terms than those granted to similarly situated executive officers. Any Awards, if granted, shall be subject to the terms of this Agreement, including Sections 5(c) and 5(d) in the event of termination or a Change in Control. (c) Annual Bonus . The CFO shall be eligible for a target annual cash bonus equal to 100% of his annual Base Salary each year (the “Annual Bonus”), to be determined by the Compensation Committee of the Board based on achievement of performance objectives, which shall be established in good faith and shall be reasonably attainable based on the Company’s business plan and market conditions. Any Annual Bonus earned shall be paid no later than March 15 of the year following the applicable performance year. (d) Travel and Entertainment . The CFO shall be reimbursed by the Company for all reasonable business, promotional, travel and entertainment expenses incurred or paid by the CFO during the Term in the performance of his services under this Agreement in accordance with the Company’s reimbursement policy. (e) Benefits and Paid Time Off . During the Term, the CFO shall be entitled to participate in all employee benefit plans, programs, and arrangements made available by the Company to similarly situated executive officers, including, without limitation, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, and retirement benefit plans, subject to the terms and conditions of such plans as may be amended from time to time. The CFO shall also be entitled to four (4) weeks of paid vacation per calendar year, accrued and administered in accordance with Company policy, together with paid holidays and sick leave provided by the Company or required under applicable law. (f) Insurance . The Company shall provide the CFO with D&O insurance commensurate with public companies of the same size and scale, on terms no less favorable than those provided to any other officer or director of the Company, and shall maintain such coverage (including any run-off or “tail” coverage) for the CFO for not less than six (6) years following the termination of his employment for any reason. (g) Promotion Option Grant . In connection with the CFO’s promotion to Chief Financial Officer, on or as soon as practicable following the Effective Date, the Company shall grant the CFO an option to purchase 170,000 ordinary shares of the Company under the Plan (the “Promotion Option”), with an exercise price per share equal to the fair market value of an ordinary share on the date of grant and a term of ten (10) years. The Promotion Option shall vest in eighteen (18) substantially equal monthly installments on each monthly anniversary of the date of grant, subject to the CFO’s continued employment through each vesting date, and shall otherwise be subject to the terms of the Plan and the applicable award agreement and to Sections 5(c) and 5(d) of this Agreement. The Promotion Option shall be in addition to, and shall not reduce, any Awards under Section 2(b). 3. Term . The terms set forth in this Agreement will commence on the Effective Date and shall remain in effect for twelve (12) months (the “ Term ”) unless earlier terminated as otherwise provided in Section 4 below. The Term shall automatically renew for additional six (6)-month periods (each, the “ Term ” or the “ Renewal Term ”), unless earlier terminated as otherwise provided in Section 4 below or either party provides written notice of its intention not to renew at least twenty-one (21) days before the expiration of the Term. Notwithstanding the above, CFO acknowledges and agrees that CFO’s employment status is that of an employee-at-will and that CFO’s employment may be terminated by either CFO or the Company at any time with or without Cause, subject to the obligations provided in Sections 4 and 5 below. For avoidance of doubt, the Term describes the intended contractual compensation and benefit framework and does not alter the at-will nature of the employment relationship. A notice of non-renewal by the Company shall be treated as a termination Without Cause for purposes of Section 5. 4. Termination . (a) Termination at the Company’s Election . (i) For Cause . At the election of the Company, CFO’s employment and this Agreement may be terminated for Cause immediately upon written notice to CFO. “Cause” shall mean the occurrence of any of the following events, as reasonably determined by the Company and/or the Board acting in good faith: (i) the willful refusal by CFO to perform his material duties or obligations under this Agreement or to follow lawful directions received by CFO from the Board; (ii) any grossly negligent act by CFO having the effect of materially injuring (whether financially or otherwise) the business or reputation of the Company or any willful act by CFO intended to cause such material injury, except any acts (A) made by CFO in connection with the enforcement of his rights, whether under this Agreement, any other agreement between the Company or any affiliate and CFO, or pursuant to applicable law (e.g. disparagement, etc.) or (B) which are required by law or pursuant to a subpoena or demand by a governmental or regulatory body; (iii) CFO’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, any felony involving moral turpitude; (iv) the determination, after a reasonable and good-faith investigation by a third-party or law firm engaged by the Company, that the CFO engaged in discrimination prohibited by law (including, without limitation, age, sex or race discrimination); (v) CFO’s material misappropriation or embezzlement of the property of the Company or its affiliates (whether or not a misdemeanor or felony); or (vi) material breach by CFO of this Agreement and/or of the Company’s confidential information or other non-disclosure agreement to which CFO is a party; provided, however, that, any such termination of CFO shall only be deemed for Cause pursuant to this definition if: (1) the Company gives the CFO written notice of the condition(s) alleged to constitute Cause, which notice shall describe such condition(s); and (2) the CFO fails to remedy such condition(s) (if curable) within thirty (30) days following receipt of the written notice. 2 (ii) Upon Disability, Death or Without Cause . At the election of the Company, CFO’s employment and this Agreement may be terminated without Cause: (A) should CFO, by reason of any medically determinable physical or mental impairment, become unable to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation, the essential functions of his job for the Company hereunder and such incapacity has continued for a total of ninety (90) consecutive days or for any one hundred eighty (180) days in a period of three hundred sixty-five (365) consecutive days (a “Disability”); (B) upon CFO’s death (“Death”); or (C) upon 21 days’ written notice to CFO for any other reason or for no reason at all (“Without Cause”). (b) Termination by CFO. (i) Voluntary Resignation . Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Agreement to the contrary, CFO may terminate his employment hereunder at any time and for any reason whatsoever or for no reason at all in CFO’s sole discretion by giving 21 days’ written notice to the Company pursuant to Section 10 (“Voluntary Resignation”). (ii) For Good Reason . At the election of the CFO, CFO’s employment and this Agreement may be terminated for Good Reason upon written notice to the Company. For purposes of this Agreement, and subject to the caveat at the end of this Section, “Good Reason” for CFO to terminate his employment hereunder shall mean the occurrence of any of the following events without CFO’s prior written consent: (i) any reduction by the Company of CFO’s Base Salary as initially set forth herein or as the same may be increased from time to time, provided, however, that if such reduction is less than 15% and occurs in connection with a Company-wide decrease in employee compensation, such reduction shall not constitute Good Reason for CFO to terminate his employment; (ii) a material breach by the Company (or any of its affiliates) of this Agreement or any other written agreement between the Company or any of its affiliates and CFO; (iii) a material adverse change in CFO’s duties, titles, authority, responsibilities or reporting relationships, with such determination being made with reference to the greatest extent of CFO’s duties, titles, authority, responsibilities or reporting relationships, etc. as increased (but not decreased) from time to time; (iv) any failure of the Company or any affiliate to pay CFO any amount owed to CFO under this Agreement or any other written agreement, plan or program between the Company, any affiliates and CFO; (v) any reduction in CFO’s bonus eligibility; (vi) any requirement that CFO relocate or materially increase the extent of required in-office presence or regularly report to a Company office in a manner that is inconsistent with CFO’s remote work arrangement described in Section 1; or (vii) any requirement that the CFO take any action, or execute any certification, filing or representation (including any certification under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002), that the CFO reasonably and in good faith believes to be false, misleading or in violation of applicable law. Provided, however, that, any such termination by the CFO shall only be deemed for Good Reason pursuant to this definition if: (1) the CFO gives the Company written notice of his intent to terminate for Good Reason; which notice shall describe such condition(s); (2) the Company fails to remedy such condition(s) within thirty (30) days following receipt of the written notice (the “Cure Period”); and (3) CFO voluntarily terminates his employment within thirty (30) days following the end of the Cure Period. 5. Payments Upon Termination of Employment . (a) Termination for Cause or Voluntary Resignation . If CFO’s employment is terminated by the Company for Cause or is terminated by CFO as a Voluntary Resignation, then the Company shall pay or provide to CFO the following amounts only: (i) his Base Salary accrued up to and including the date of termination or resignation, paid within thirty (30) days or at such earlier time required by applicable law; (ii) any deferred compensation earned but unpaid as of the date of termination; (iii) unreimbursed expenses, paid in accordance with this Agreement and the Company’s written policies; (iv) any accrued but unpaid Annual Bonus; and (v) accrued benefits under any Company benefit plan, paid pursuant to the terms of such benefit plan (collectively, the “Accrued Obligations”). (b) Termination Without Cause or for Good Reason. Except as provided in Section 5(c), if the Company terminates CFO’s employment Without Cause or because of CFO’s Death or Disability, or CFO terminates for Good Reason, in addition to the Accrued Obligations, the Company shall provide CFO, or his estate, severance in the form of continuation of his salary (at the Base Salary rate in effect at the time of termination, but prior to any reduction triggering Good Reason) for twelve (12) months following the termination date. CFO shall also receive a prorated target Annual Bonus for the year in which termination occurs and reimbursement of COBRA premiums for up to twelve (12) months following termination. The severance and prorated target Annual Bonus payments will be subject to standard payroll deductions and withholdings and will be made on the Company’s regular payroll cycle, provided, however, that such payments are subject to CFO’s execution and delivery of a general release (that is no longer subject to revocation under applicable law) of the Company, its parents, subsidiaries and affiliates and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors and assigns in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Company. All payments under this Section above shall begin to be made within sixty (60) days following termination of employment; provided, however, that to the extent required by Code Section 409A (as defined below), if the sixty (60) day period begins in one calendar year and ends in the second calendar year, all payments will be made in the second calendar year. The payments under this Section 5(b) shall immediately cease should CFO materially violate any of the obligations set forth in Sections 6 and 7 below. 3 (c) Change in Control Protection . Upon a Change in Control of the Company, and if the CFO’s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause or by the CFO for Good Reason within twelve (12) months following such Change in Control, the CFO shall be entitled to receive: (i) twelve (12) months of Base Salary continuation; (ii) a prorated target Annual Bonus for the year of termination; (iii) payment or reimbursement of COBRA premiums for up to twelve (12) months; and (iv) full vesting of all outstanding unvested equity awards held by the CFO. The severance and prorated bonus payments will be subject to standard payroll deductions and withholdings and will be made on the Company’s regular payroll cycle, subject to the CFO’s execution and delivery of a general release of claims in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Company. The benefits provided under this Section 5(c) shall be in lieu of, and not in addition to, the salary continuation, prorated target Annual Bonus and COBRA benefits provided under Section 5(b), and shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any benefits otherwise payable under Section 5(d) or any applicable equity award agreement or the Plan. The payments under this Section 5(c) shall be made at the times, and shall be subject to the conditions, set forth in Section 5(b). For purposes of this Agreement, “Change in Control” shall have the meaning given to the term “Change of Control” in the Plan as in effect on the Effective Date, and any amendment, successor plan, or transaction document shall not be used to broaden, narrow, or otherwise modify such definition with respect to the CFO without the CFO’s prior written consent. (d) Equity Treatment . In the event the CFO’s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause, due to the CFO’s Death or Disability, or by the CFO for Good Reason, any outstanding unvested equity awards held by the CFO shall immediately vest as to the portion of such awards that would have vested during the twelve (12) months following the date of termination, determined as if the CFO had remained continuously employed through such twelve (12) month period, and notwithstanding any requirement of continued service as a condition to vesting, and regardless of any contrary vesting or forfeiture provisions set forth in the Plan or any applicable equity award agreement. Any vested stock options shall remain exercisable for a period of not less than twelve (12) months following termination, subject to the terms of the applicable equity award agreements and the Plan. For clarity, the provisions of this Section 5(d) shall apply independently of, and shall supersede to the extent more favorable to the CFO, any terms contained in the Plan or any individual equity award agreement. 6. Restrictive Covenants . The CFO acknowledges and agrees that (i) the CFO has a major responsibility for the operation, development and growth of the Company’s business; (ii) the CFO’s work for the Company will bring him into close contact with Confidential Information (defined below) of the Company and its clients; and (iii) the agreements and covenants contained in this Section 6 are essential to protect the legitimate business interests of the Company and that the Company will not enter into this Employment Agreement but for such agreements and covenants. Accordingly, the CFO covenants and agrees to the following: (a) Confidential Information . (i) CFO understands that during his employment and under this Agreement, he may have access to unpublished and otherwise confidential information both of a technical and non-technical nature, relating to the business of the Company or any of its parents, subsidiaries, divisions, affiliates (collectively, “Affiliated Entities”), or clients, including without limitation any of their actual or anticipated business, research or development, any of their technology or the implementation or exploitation thereof, including without limitation information CFO and others have collected, obtained or created, information pertaining to clients, accounts, vendors, prices, costs, materials, processes, codes, material results, technology, system designs, system specifications, materials of construction, trade secrets or equipment designs, including information disclosed to the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities by others under agreements to hold such information confidential (collectively, the “Confidential Information”). CFO agrees to observe all policies and procedures of the Company and its Affiliated Entities concerning such Confidential Information. CFO further agrees not to disclose or use, either during his employment or at any time thereafter, any Confidential Information for any purpose, including without limitation any competitive purpose, unless authorized to do so by the Company in writing, except that he may disclose and use such information in the good faith performance of his duties for the Company. CFO’s obligations under this Employment Agreement will continue with respect to Confidential Information, whether or not his employment is terminated, until such information becomes generally available from public sources through no fault of CFO or any representative of CFO. Notwithstanding the foregoing, however, CFO shall be permitted to disclose Confidential Information as may be required by a subpoena or other governmental order, provided that he first notifies the Company of such subpoena, order or other requirement and such that the Company has the opportunity to obtain a protective order or other appropriate remedy. 4 (ii) During CFO’s employment, upon the Company’s request, or upon the termination of his employment for any reason, CFO will promptly deliver to the Company all documents, records, files, notebooks, manuals, letters, notes, reports, client information and lists, cost and profit data, e-mail, apparatus, laptops, computers, smartphones, tablets or other PDAs, hardware, software, drawings, blueprints, and any other material of the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities or clients, including all materials pertaining to Confidential Information developed by CFO or others, and all copies of such materials, whether of a technical, business or fiscal nature, whether on the hard drive of a laptop or desktop computer, in hard copy, disk or any other format, which are in his possession, custody or control. (b) Non-Solicitation . During the Term and for a period of one year after employment, CFO shall not: (i) solicit or induce, or attempt to solicit or induce, any employee of the Company to leave the employ of the Company; or (ii) solicit or attempt to solicit the business of any client or customer of the Company with respect to products, services, or investments similar to those provided or supplied by the Company. (c) CFO agrees that if the duration of, the scope of or any business activity covered by any provision of this Section 6 is in excess of what is determined to be valid and enforceable under applicable law, such provision shall be construed to cover only that duration, scope or activity that is determined to be valid and enforceable. CFO hereby acknowledges that this Section 6 shall be given the construction that renders its provisions valid and enforceable to the maximum extent, not exceeding its express terms, possible under applicable law. 7. Representations, Warranties and Covenants of the CFO . (a) No Restrictive Covenants . CFO represents and warrants to the Company that he is not subject to any agreement restricting his ability to enter into this Agreement and fully carry out his duties and responsibilities hereunder. (b) Assignment of Intellectual Property . (i) CFO will promptly disclose to the Company any idea, invention, discovery or improvement, whether patentable or not (“Creations”), conceived or made by him alone or with others at any time during his employment with the Company. CFO agrees that the Company owns any such Creations, and CFO hereby assigns and agrees to assign to the Company all moral and other rights he has or may acquire therein and agrees to execute any and all applications, assignments and other instruments relating thereto which the Company deems necessary or desirable. These obligations shall continue beyond the termination of his employment with respect to Creations and derivatives of such Creations conceived or made during his employment with the Company. The Company and CFO understand that the obligation to assign Creations to the Company shall not apply to any Creation which is developed entirely on his own time without using any of the Company’s equipment, supplies, facilities, and/or Confidential Information (“CFO Creations”) unless such Creation (i) relates in any way to the business or to the current or anticipated research or development of the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities, or (ii) results in any way from his work at the Company. (ii) In any jurisdiction in which moral rights cannot be assigned, CFO hereby waives any such moral rights and any similar or analogous rights under the applicable laws of any country of the world that CFO may have in connection with the Creations, and to the extent such waiver is unenforceable, hereby covenants and agrees not to bring any claim, suit or other legal proceeding against the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities claiming that CFO’s moral rights to the Creations have been violated. (iii) CFO agrees to reasonably cooperate with the Company, both during and after his employment with the Company, with respect to the procurement, maintenance and enforcement of copyrights, patents, trademarks and other intellectual property rights (both in the United States and foreign countries) relating to such Creations. CFO shall sign all papers, including, without limitation, copyright applications, patent applications, declarations, oaths, formal assignments, assignments of priority rights and powers of attorney, which the Company, acting reasonably, may deem necessary or desirable in order to protect its rights and interests in any Creations. CFO further agrees that if the Company is unable, after reasonable effort, to secure CFO’s signature on any such papers, any officer of the Company shall be entitled to execute such papers as his agent and attorney-in-fact and CFO hereby irrevocably designates and appoints each officer of the Company as his agent and attorney-in-fact to execute any such papers on his behalf and to take any and all actions as the Company may deem necessary or desirable in order to protect its rights and interests in any Creations, under the conditions described in this paragraph, all to the exclusion of CFO’s Creations. 5 8. Remedies . The CFO acknowledges that the Company would be irreparably injured by a violation of the covenants contained in Sections 6 or 7, and agrees that the Company shall be entitled to an injunction restraining the CFO from any actual or threatened breach of the covenants contained in Sections 6 or 7, or to any other appropriate equitable remedy without bond or other security being required. Any such relief shall be in addition to and not in lieu of any appropriate relief in the way of monetary damages that the parties may seek in arbitration. 9. Waiver of Breach . The waiver by either the Company or the CFO of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate as or be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach by either the Company or the CFO. Any waiver must be in writing. 10. Notice . Any notice to be given hereunder by a party hereto shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been given when received or, when deposited in the U.S. mail, certified or registered mail, postage prepaid: (a) to the CFO, at the address on file with the Company. (b) to the Company addressed as follows: Quantum Cyber N.V. 38 Union Avenue Bridgeport, CT 06607 11. Amendment . This Agreement may not be amended orally in any manner or in writing without the written consent of the Company and the CFO. No provision of this Agreement may be waived, delayed, modified, terminated or otherwise impaired without the prior written consent of the Company and the CFO. 12. Entire Agreement . This Agreement embodies the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto in respect of the CFO’s employment with the Company contemplated by this Agreement and supersedes all prior agreements, arrangements and understandings, oral or written, express or implied, between the parties with respect to such employment; provided, however, that nothing herein shall adversely affect any compensation earned, equity granted (including the shares granted under Section 2(d) of the Prior Agreement), or rights to indemnification, advancement of expenses or D&O coverage accrued under the Employment Agreement between the Company and the CFO dated June 1, 2026 (the “Prior Agreement”), and the CFO’s service under the Prior Agreement shall count as service for all purposes under this Agreement, including vesting, benefits and paid time off. Sections 5, 6, 7, 19 and 20 of this Agreement shall survive the termination of this Agreement. 13. Applicable Law . The provisions of this Agreement shall be construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware. 14. Assignment; Successors and Assigns, etc . This Agreement is a personal contract and CFO may not sell, transfer, assign, pledge or hypothecate his rights, interests and obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise herein expressly provided, this Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of CFO and his personal representatives and shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Company and its successors and assigns, except that the Company may not assign this Agreement without CFO’s prior written consent, except to an acquirer of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company. 15. Enforceability . If any portion or provision of this Agreement (including, without limitation, any portion or provision of any section of this Agreement) shall to any extent be declared illegal or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, then the remainder of this Agreement, or the application of such portion or provision in circumstances other than those as to which it is so declared illegal or unenforceable, shall not be affected thereby, and each portion and provision of this Agreement shall be valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law. 16. Counterparts; Construction . This Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall be considered one and the same agreement and shall become effective when one or more counterparts have been signed by each of the parties and delivered to the other party. Facsimile or .pdf signatures shall have the same force and effect as original signatures. This Agreement shall not be construed more strictly against one Party than the other, merely by virtue of the fact that it may have been prepared by counsel for one of the Parties, it being recognized that both Company and CFO have contributed substantially and materially to the negotiation and preparation of this Agreement. In construing this Agreement, the singular shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular, and the use of any gender shall include every other and all genders. 6 17. Section 409A Compliance . The intent of the Parties is that payments and benefits under this Agreement comply with, or be exempt from, Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”) and the regulations and guidance promulgated thereunder (collectively “Code Section 409A”) and, accordingly, to the maximum extent permitted, this Agreement shall be interpreted and administered accordingly. A termination of employment shall not be deemed to have occurred for purposes of any provision of this Agreement providing for the payment of any amounts or benefits upon or following a termination of employment that are considered “nonqualified deferred compensation” under Code Section 409A unless such termination is also a “separation from service” within the meaning of Code Section 409A and, for purposes of any such provision of this Agreement, references to a “termination,” “termination of employment” or like terms shall mean “separation from service.” With regard to any provision herein that provides for reimbursement of costs and expenses or in-kind benefits, except as permitted by Code Section 409A, (i) the right to reimbursement or in-kind benefits shall not be subject to liquidation or exchange for another benefit, (ii) the amount of expenses eligible for reimbursement, or in-kind benefits, provided during any taxable year shall not affect the expenses eligible for reimbursement, or in-kind benefits to be provided, in any other taxable year, provided that the foregoing clause (ii) shall not be violated without regard to expenses reimbursed under any arrangement covered by Code Section 105(b) solely because such expenses are subject to a limit related to the period the arrangement is in effect and (iii) such payments shall be made on or before the last day of CFO’s taxable year following the taxable year in which the expense occurred. For purposes of Code Section 409A, CFO’s right to receive any installment payments pursuant to this Agreement shall be treated as a right to receive a series of separate and distinct payments. Whenever a payment under this Agreement specifies a payment period with reference to a number of days (e.g., “within sixty (60) days following the date of termination”), the actual date of payment within the specified period shall be within the sole discretion of the Company. If CFO is a specified employee within the meaning of Code Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) and would receive any payment sooner than 6 months after CFO’s “separation from service” that, absent the application of this Section 17, would be subject to additional tax imposed pursuant to Code Section 409A as a result of such status as a specified employee, then such payment shall instead be payable on the date that is the earliest of (i) 6 months after CFO’s “separation from service,” or (ii) CFO’s death. 18. Section 280G . In the event that any payments, distributions, benefits or entitlements of any type payable to CFO (the “Total Payments”) would (i) constitute “parachute payments” within the meaning of Section 280G of the Code (which will not include any portion of payments allocated to the restrictive covenant provisions of Section 6 hereof that are classified as payments of reasonable compensation for purposes of Section 280G of the Code), and (ii) but for this paragraph would be subject to the excise tax imposed by Section 4999 of the Code (the “Excise Tax”), then the Total Payments shall be either: (a) provided in full, or (b) provided as to such lesser extent as would result in no portion of such Total Payments being subject to the Excise Tax, whichever of the foregoing amounts, taking into account the applicable federal, state and local income taxes and the Excise Tax, results in CFO’s receipt on an after-tax basis of the greatest amount of the Total Payments, notwithstanding that all or some portion of the Total Payments may be subject to the Excise Tax. Unless the Company and CFO otherwise agree in writing, any determination required under this Section 18 shall be made in writing in good faith based on the advice of a nationally recognized accounting firm selected by the Company (with approval of CFO) (the “Accountants”). In the event of a reduction of benefits hereunder, benefits shall be reduced by first reducing or eliminating the portion of the Total Payments that are payable in cash under Section 2(c) or Section 5 and then by reducing or eliminating any amounts that are payable with respect to long-term incentives including any equity-based or equity-related awards (whether payable in cash or in kind). For purposes of making the calculations required by this Section 18, the Accountants may make reasonable assumptions and approximations concerning applicable taxes and may rely on reasonable, good faith interpretations concerning the application of the Code, and other applicable legal authority. The Company and CFO shall furnish to the Accountants such information and documents as the Accountants may reasonably require to make a determination under this Section 18, and the Company shall bear the cost of all fees the Accountants charge in connection with any calculations contemplated by this Section 18. 19. Arbitration . All disputes and disagreements arising from, relating to, or otherwise connected with this Agreement, the breach of this Agreement, the enforcement, interpretation or validity of this Agreement, or the employment relationship (including any wage claim, claim for wrongful termination, or any claim based upon any statute, regulation, or law, including those dealing with employment discrimination or retaliation, sexual harassment, civil rights, age, or disability) that the Company may have against CFO or that CFO may have against the Company, including the determination of the scope or applicability of this Agreement to arbitrate, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services (“JAMS”) pursuant to its Employment Arbitration Rules and Procedures applicable at the time the arbitration is commenced (“JAMS Rules”). A copy of the current version of the JAMS Rules will be made available to the CFO upon request. The Rules may be amended from time to time and are also available online https://www.jamsadr.com/rules-employment-arbitration/. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the parties. Judgment on any award may be entered in any court having competent jurisdiction, and application may be made to such court for a judicial acceptance of the award and an order of enforcement, as the case may be. The Company shall bear all arbitrator fees and administrative costs of the arbitration except for any filing fee that the CFO would have been required to pay had the claim been filed in a court of competent jurisdiction. In any action to enforce this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs, and expenses. 20. Indemnification . The Company shall defend and indemnify CFO in his capacity as CFO of the Company and as an officer, director or employee of any of its subsidiaries to the fullest extent permitted under the laws of the Company’s domicile, including the laws of the Company’s jurisdiction of incorporation and the Company’s articles of association, and shall advance reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses as incurred, subject to an undertaking to repay such amounts if it is ultimately determined that the CFO is not entitled to indemnification. The Company shall also maintain a policy for indemnifying its officers and directors, including but not limited to the CFO, for all actions permitted under applicable law taken in good faith pursuit of their duties for the Company, including but not limited to maintaining an appropriate level of Directors and Officers Liability coverage and maintaining the inclusion of such provisions in the Company’s by-laws or articles of incorporation, as applicable and customary. The rights to indemnification shall survive any termination of this Agreement. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank] 7 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the CFO and the Company have executed this Agreement as of the date first above written. /s/ David Caplon David Caplon Quantum Cyber N.V. text: EX-10.2 2 ea031299601ex10-2.htm AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE SOLIDION TECHNOLOGY, INC. 2023 EQUITY INCENTIVE PLAN Exhibit 10.2 AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE 2023 EQUITY INCENTIVE PLAN APPENDIX A The Board of Directors of SOLIDION TECHNOLOGY, INC., a Delaware corporation, does hereby certify the amendment of the Solidion Technology, Inc. 2023 Equity Incentive Plan (the “Stock Plan”), effective September 23, 2026, subject to stockholders’ approval, as follows: 1. Section 2 of the Plan is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: 2. Shares Subject to the Plan. (a) Share Reserve. Subject to any adjustments as necessary to implement any Capitalization Adjustments and the provisions of 2(b), the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock that may be issued pursuant to Awards will not exceed an amount equal to 1,489,908 shares of Common Stock, after giving effect to the 1-for-50 reverse stock split effected by the Company on May 12, 2025 (the “2025 Reverse Split”). (b) Share Reserve Operation. (i) Automatic Share Reserve Increase. Subject to any adjustments as necessary to implement any Capitalization Adjustments, the number of shares of Common Stock available for issuance under the Plan will be increased on the first day of each fiscal year beginning with the 2027 fiscal year, in an amount equal to the least of (1) 190,000 shares (after giving effect to the 2025 Reverse Split) of Common Stock, (2) a number of shares of Common Stock equal to five percent (5%) of the total number of shares of all classes of common stock of the Company outstanding on the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal year, or (3) such number of shares of Common Stock determined by the Plan administrator no later than the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal year. (ii) Actions that Do Not Constitute Issuance of Common Stock and Do Not Reduce Share Reserve. The following actions do not result in an issuance of shares under the Plan and accordingly do not reduce the number of shares subject to the Share Reserve and available for issuance under the Plan: (1) the expiration or termination of any portion of an Award without the shares covered by such portion of the Award having been issued; and (2) the settlement of any portion of an Award in cash (i.e., the Participant receives cash rather than Common Stock). (iii) Reversion of Previously Issued Shares of Common Stock to Share Reserve. Any shares of Common Stock previously issued pursuant to an Award that are forfeited back to or repurchased by the Company because of a failure to meet a contingency or condition required for the vesting of such shares of Common Stock and accordingly initially deducted from the Share Reserve will be added back to the Share Reserve and again become available for issuance under the Plan.

text: EX-10.1 2 ea031310701ex10-1.htm AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER AGREEMENT OF CERTAIN APITOX RIGHTS, DATED NOVEMBER 12, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN APIMEDS PHARMACEUTICALS US, INC. AND FREET INC Exhibit 10.1 AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER AGREEMENT OF CERTAIN APITOX RIGHTS This Amendment No. 1 (this “ Amendment ”) to the Assignment and Transfer Agreement of Certain Apitox Rights is entered into as of November 12, 2026 (the “ Amendment Date ”) by and between FreeT Inc., a company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea (formerly known as Inscobee Co., Ltd. and CNP Roen Co., Ltd.) (“ FreeT ” or the “ Assignor ”), and APIMEDS PHARMACEUTICALS US, INC., a Delaware corporation (“ APUS ” or the “ Assignee ”). FreeT and APUS are referred to collectively as the “ Parties ” and individually as a “ Party .” RECITALS WHEREAS, the Parties entered into the Assignment and Transfer Agreement of Certain Apitox Rights executed on August 19, 2026 (the “ Agreement ”), pursuant to which FreeT assigned and transferred the Assigned Rights to APUS; WHEREAS, Article 7.1 of the Agreement provides that any additional monetary or other consideration shall be set forth in a separate written agreement signed by the Parties; WHEREAS, the Parties have agreed that the consideration for the Assigned Rights shall consist of an initial issuance of 350,000 shares of common stock of APUS, together with such additional consideration, if any, as is determined on the basis of a valuation of the Assigned Rights by an independent third-party valuer; WHEREAS, the Parties wish to amend Article 7 of the Agreement to record the foregoing, in accordance with Article 9.2 of the Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Definitions 1.1 Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment have the meanings given to them in the Agreement. 1.2 The Parties confirm that the “Effective Date” of the Agreement is August 19, 2026. 2. Amendment of Article 7 (Consideration) 2.1 Article 7 of the Agreement is hereby deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: “Article 7. Consideration 7.1 Consideration. In consideration of the assignment and transfer of the Assigned Rights, APUS shall provide to FreeT (a) the Initial Consideration in accordance with Article 7.2 and (b) the Additional Consideration, if any, in accordance with Articles 7.3 to 7.5 (together, the “ Total Consideration ”). 7.2 Initial Consideration. APUS shall issue to FreeT 350,000 shares of common stock of APUS, par value US$0.001 per share (“ Common Stock ”, and such shares, the “ Initial Shares ”), no later than December 1, 2026. The Initial Shares, when issued, shall be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable. 7.3 Independent Valuation. (a) Within sixty (60) days after the Amendment Date, the Parties shall jointly appoint an independent third-party valuer of recognized standing with experience in the valuation of pharmaceutical and life-sciences rights (the “ Independent Valuer ”). If the Parties fail to agree on the Independent Valuer within such period, parties shall jointly select the Independent Valuer. (b) The Independent Valuer shall determine the fair value of the Assigned Rights as of the Effective Date (the “ Final Valuation ”) and shall deliver a written valuation report to both Parties within sixty (60) days after its appointment. (c) Each Party shall provide the Independent Valuer with such information and assistance as it may reasonably request. The Final Valuation shall be final and binding on the Parties, save in the case of fraud or manifest error. (d) The fees and expenses of the Independent Valuer shall be borne by the Parties in equal shares. 7.4 Additional Consideration. If the Final Valuation exceeds the Initial Consideration Value, APUS shall pay to FreeT an amount equal to such excess (the “ Additional Consideration ”) within thirty (30) days after delivery of the valuation report, subject to Article 7.6. The Additional Consideration may be paid, at the election of APUS, in cash, in shares of Common Stock, or in any combination thereof. 7.5 No Downward Adjustment. If the Final Valuation is equal to or less than the Initial Consideration Value, no Additional Consideration shall be payable, and FreeT shall retain the Initial Shares without adjustment, return or refund. 2 7.6 Approvals and Legal Compliance. The issuance of the Initial Shares and any Additional Shares is subject to (a) approval by the board of directors of APUS and any other corporate approval required of APUS, and (b) compliance with applicable law, including United States federal and state securities laws and the rules of the principal securities exchange on which the Common Stock is listed. If any Additional Shares cannot be issued without stockholder approval or without contravening such laws or rules, APUS shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain such approval, failing which it shall pay the corresponding portion of the Additional Consideration in cash. 7.7 Securities Law Matters. FreeT acknowledges that the Initial Shares and any Additional Shares (a) have not been registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “ Securities Act ”), or any state securities laws, (b) will be issued in reliance on an exemption from registration, (c) will constitute “restricted securities” bearing a customary restrictive legend, and (d) may not be offered, sold or transferred except pursuant to an effective registration statement or an available exemption, including Rule 144 under the Securities Act. APUS has no obligation to register any such shares. As a condition to each issuance, FreeT shall deliver such customary investor representations and documents as APUS may reasonably request. APUS makes no representation as to the date on which any holding period under Rule 144 commences. 7.8 Entire Consideration; Taxes. The Total Consideration constitutes the full and entire consideration payable by APUS in respect of the Assigned Rights, and no other payment, issuance or consideration shall be due from APUS to FreeT under this Agreement. Each Party shall bear its own taxes arising in connection with the Total Consideration, and APUS may deduct and withhold any amounts required to be withheld under applicable law.” 3. Assignment Unaffected 3.1 The Parties confirm that the assignment and transfer of the Assigned Rights under Article 2 of the Agreement took effect on the Effective Date and remains in full force and effect. Such assignment and transfer is not conditional upon, and shall not be affected by, the Final Valuation, the timing or outcome of the valuation process, or any dispute concerning the Additional Consideration. 4. Representations 4.1 Each Party represents and warrants to the other that it has full corporate power and authority to enter into and perform this Amendment, and that the execution of this Amendment has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action of such Party. 3 5. Effect of Amendment 5.1 Except as expressly amended by this Amendment, the Agreement remains unchanged and in full force and effect. From the Amendment Date, the Agreement and this Amendment shall be read and construed as a single instrument, and references in the Agreement to “this Agreement” shall mean the Agreement as amended by this Amendment. 5.2 In the event of any conflict between this Amendment and the Agreement, this Amendment shall prevail. 5.3 This Amendment constitutes the “separate written agreement” contemplated by Article 7.1 of the Agreement as originally executed, and supersedes all prior discussions and understandings between the Parties concerning the consideration for the Assigned Rights. 6. Governing Law; Dispute Resolution 6.1 Article 8 (Governing Law; Dispute Resolution) of the Agreement applies to this Amendment as if set out in full herein. 7. Counterparts 7.1 This Amendment may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one instrument. SIGNATURE PAGE FOLLOWS 4 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Amendment as of the Amendment Date. FreeT Inc. APIMEDS PHARMACEUTICALS US, INC. By: /s/ Byung Kwon Song By: /s/ Dr. Vin Menon Name: Byung Kwon Song Name: Dr. Vin Menon Title: Chief Executive Officer Title: Co-Chief Executive Officer By: /s/ Sung Joon Chae Name: Sung Joon Chae Title: Co-Chief Executive Officer 5

text: EX-10.1 2 ea031312601ex10-1.htm FORM OF SERIES C PREFERRED STOCK REPURCHASE AGREEMENT Exhibit 10.1 SERIES C PREFERRED STOCK REPURCHASE AGREEMENT This Preferred Stock Repurchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into effective this 16th day of November, 2026, by and between Greenland Mines Ltd. (the “Company”) and the Series C Preferred stockholder shown on the signature page hereto (“Stockholder”). WITNESSETH: WHEREAS, the Stockholder currently owns such number of shares of the Company’s Series C Preferred Stock as are set forth on the signature page hereto (the “Shares”); WHEREAS, the Stockholder desires that the Company repurchase all of Stockholder’s Shares at the purchase price on the terms and conditions set forth herein (the “Repurchase”). NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing premises, mutual agreements and covenants herein set forth, and for other valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto, intending to be legally bound hereby, agree as follows: 1. Repurchase. Subject to the terms and conditions contained herein, effective as of the date hereof, the Stockholder hereby sells, assigns and transfers the Shares to the Company for the repurchase price set forth below, and agrees to deliver to the Company the stock power attached hereto duly executed in blank (the “Stock Power”). 2. Repurchase Price . The Company shall pay to the Stockholder the sum of $1,276.62 per share as the repurchase price for the Shares. 3. Representations and Warranties of the Stockholder. The Stockholder hereby represents and warrants to the Company that the Stockholder: (a) has full legal right, power and capacity to (i) execute and deliver this Agreement and the Stock Power, and (ii) to perform its obligations hereunder and thereunder; (b) owns the Shares free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, and claims of others, and has the right to transfer, sell and deliver the Shares to the Company for repurchase in accordance with the terms of this Agreement; and (c) has such knowledge of the business and financial affairs of the Company and possesses a sufficient degree of sophistication, knowledge and experience in financial and business matters such that they are capable of evaluating the sale of the Shares and the economic risks of selling the same to the Company. 4. Further Assurances. The Stockholder shall execute and deliver such additional instruments and documents as may reasonably be requested by the Company, in order to carry out the purposes and intent of this Agreement and to fulfill the obligations of the Stockholder under this Agreement. 5. Entire Agreement. This Agreement (along with the documents referred to in this Agreement) contains the entire understanding and agreement of the parties with respect to the transaction covered hereby and supersedes all other understandings and agreements between the parties, oral or written, relating to the subject matter of this Agreement. No modification, alteration, or amendment of this Agreement and no wavier of any provision of this Agreement shall be valid or effective unless in writing executed by the Company and the Stockholder. 6. Binding Agreement. This Agreement shall be binding upon, inure to the benefit of, and apply to the respective heirs, personal representatives, successors, and the assigns of the parties hereto. 7. Construction. This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the substantive laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflicts of laws principles. The language of all parts of this Agreement shall in all cases be construed as a whole, according to its fair meaning, and not strictly for or against any of the signatory parties. 8. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which will be deemed to be an original copy of this Agreement and all of which, when taken together, will be deemed to constitute one and the same agreement. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement the day and year first above written. text: EX-10.1 2 ea031282601ex10-1.htm CONVERTIBLE PROMISSORY NOTE, DATED AS OF NOVEMBER 17, 2026, ISSUED BY VENHUB GLOBAL, INC. TO MERIDIAN EQUITY VENTURES, LLC Exhibit 10.1 NEITHER THIS NOTE NOR THE SECURITIES ISSUABLE UPON CONVERSION HAVE BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”), OR ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS, AND THEY MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD OR TRANSFERRED EXCEPT PURSUANT TO AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT OR AN AVAILABLE EXEMPTION FROM REGISTRATION, AS EVIDENCED, IF REQUESTED BY THE COMPANY, BY AN OPINION OF COUNSEL REASONABLY ACCEPTABLE TO THE COMPANY. VENHUB GLOBAL, INC. CONVERTIBLE PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Amount: up to $2,000,000.00 Issuance Date: November 17, 2026 FOR VALUE RECEIVED, VenHub Global, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Company”), promises to pay to Meridian Equity Ventures, LLC (the “Holder”) the principal amount actually funded by the Holder under this Convertible Promissory Note (this “Note”), up to Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000.00) (the “Principal Amount”), together with interest, on the terms below. Section 1. Funding; Maturity; Interest 1.1 Tranches. The Holder shall fund the Principal Amount in four (4) equal installments of $500,000.00 each (each, a “Tranche”): the first on the Issuance Date and one on the same day of each of the three (3) consecutive calendar months thereafter (each, a “Funding Date”). The Holder’s funding obligation for any Tranche is subject to no Event of Default (as defined below) then continuing. The Holder may, by written notice to the Company, suspend funding of any subsequent Tranche if, as of the applicable Funding Date, (a) an Event of Default, or an event that with notice or lapse of time would become an Event of Default, has occurred and is continuing, (b) the Common Stock (as defined below) has been delisted from, or the Company has received written notice of delisting from, the Trading Market (as defined below), or (c) trading in the Common Stock on the Trading Market has been suspended for more than five (5) consecutive Trading Days (as defined below) during the thirty (30) days preceding such Funding Date. Any suspended Tranche shall be funded within five (5) Business Days after the applicable condition has been cured (which, in the case of clause (b), means the Common Stock remains listed on the Trading Market and any delisting notice has been withdrawn or the Company has regained compliance), unless the Holder elects otherwise. 1.2 Maturity. This Note matures on March 16, 2027 (the “Maturity Date”), on which date the outstanding Principal Amount and accrued interest shall convert into Common Stock under Section 2. 1.3 Interest. Interest accrues on each Tranche from its Funding Date at 5% per annum, computed on a 365-day year, and is paid in kind by addition to the Principal Amount. During the continuance of an Event of Default, the rate increases by five percent (5%) per annum, not to exceed the maximum rate permitted by law. Page 1 1.4 Prepayment. The Company may prepay all or part of the outstanding Principal Amount and accrued and unpaid interest at any time, without premium or penalty, on ten (10) Trading Days’ written notice. The Holder may elect, before the prepayment date, to convert the amount to be prepaid under Section 2 instead, in which case such conversion shall be subject to the same Conversion Price, delivery and other conversion terms set forth in Section 2, with references in Section 2 to the Maturity Date deemed to refer to the prepayment date. 1.5 Ranking. This Note is an unsecured general obligation of the Company. Section 2. Conversion 2.1 Automatic Conversion at Maturity. On the Maturity Date, unless earlier repaid, the outstanding Principal Amount plus accrued and unpaid interest (the “Conversion Amount”) shall automatically convert into shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.001 per share (“Common Stock”; such shares issuable upon conversion of this Note, the “Conversion Shares”), equal to the Conversion Amount divided by the Conversion Price, with the number of Conversion Shares determined as of the date the Conversion Price is determined under Section 2.2. 2.2 Conversion Price. “Conversion Price” means the lower of (a) ninety percent (90%) of the average daily VWAP of the Common Stock on the Trading Market for the five (5) Trading Days immediately preceding the Maturity Date, and (b) ninety percent (90%) of the average daily VWAP of the Common Stock on the Trading Market for the five (5) Trading Days immediately preceding the date on which the applicable shares of Common Stock are actually delivered to the Holder as freely tradable shares, either registered for resale under an effective Registration Statement (as defined in Section 3.1) or eligible for resale under Rule 144 without volume or manner-of-sale restrictions or current public information requirements (each of (a) and (b) representing a ten percent (10%) discount to market), but in no event less than the Floor Price. If registration or delivery is delayed for any reason, the Conversion Price for the affected shares shall not be determined until such shares are so delivered. If any Conversion Shares have not been so delivered within one hundred twenty (120) days after the Maturity Date (other than because of the Exchange Cap or Section 2.5), the Holder may, by written notice to the Company, elect to have the corresponding portion of the Conversion Amount repaid in cash within ten (10) Business Days after such notice. 2.3 Floor Price. “Floor Price” means $0.0414, which equals twenty percent (20%) of the Nasdaq “Minimum Price” (as defined in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d)) on the Trading Day immediately preceding the Issuance Date, subject to proportionate adjustment for stock splits, reverse splits, stock dividends and similar events. If the Conversion Price would otherwise be less than the Floor Price, the applicable portion of the Conversion Amount shall be converted at the Floor Price, and the issuance of Conversion Shares at the Floor Price shall fully satisfy the portion of the Conversion Amount so converted. The Company shall have no obligation to pay any cash or other consideration on account of any difference between the Floor Price and the price that would otherwise have applied under Section 2.2. Page 2 2.4 Nasdaq Exchange Cap; Stockholder Approval. Notwithstanding anything herein, while the Common Stock is listed on Nasdaq, the Company shall not issue any shares of Common Stock under this Note (aggregated with any other transaction that Nasdaq would aggregate with this Note) in excess of 19.99% of the shares of Common Stock outstanding immediately before the Issuance Date (the “Exchange Cap”) prior to obtaining Stockholder Approval, if and to the extent such issuance would violate the Nasdaq Listing Rules. “Stockholder Approval” means the approval of the issuance of shares of Common Stock under this Note in excess of the Exchange Cap by the Company’s stockholders, as required by Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d), obtained either at a meeting of stockholders or by written consent of the holders of a majority of the voting power of the Company’s outstanding capital stock and, if obtained by written consent, effective no earlier than twenty (20) calendar days after a definitive information statement on Schedule 14C is first mailed to stockholders in accordance with Rule 14c-2 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”). If Stockholder Approval is required, the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain it, including by filing a preliminary information statement on Schedule 14C with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) within fifteen (15) days after the Company determines that Stockholder Approval is required and mailing the definitive information statement as promptly as practicable thereafter. Any Conversion Amount that cannot be converted on the Maturity Date because of the Exchange Cap shall be converted within three (3) Trading Days after Stockholder Approval becomes effective or, if Stockholder Approval has not become effective within sixty (60) days after the Maturity Date, shall be repaid in cash within thirty (30) days thereafter. The Company shall not issue any shares under this Note in violation of any Nasdaq rule. 2.5 Beneficial Ownership Limit. The Company shall not issue Conversion Shares to the extent that, after giving effect to such issuance, the Holder and its affiliates would beneficially own (as determined under Section 13(d) of the Exchange Act) more than 9.99% of the outstanding Common Stock (the “Beneficial Ownership Limit”). If a conversion would cause the Holder to exceed the Beneficial Ownership Limit, the Company shall issue only the number of Conversion Shares that may be issued without exceeding the Beneficial Ownership Limit, and the portion of the Conversion Amount not converted as a result (the “Deferred Amount”) shall remain outstanding as a dollar amount, shall continue to accrue interest under Section 1.3, and shall not be represented by any fixed number of shares. The Deferred Amount shall convert, in whole or in part, from time to time as Conversion Shares may be issued without exceeding the Beneficial Ownership Limit, at the Conversion Price determined under Section 2.2 as of the date the corresponding freely tradable Conversion Shares are actually delivered to the Holder, and the number of Conversion Shares issuable in respect of the Deferred Amount shall be determined only at that time. The Holder shall be responsible for determining whether the Beneficial Ownership Limit applies, subject to the Company’s approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Page 3 2.6 Delivery; Fractional Shares; Late Delivery. The Company shall deliver the shares in book-entry form within three (3) Trading Days after the later of the Maturity Date and the date on which the Conversion Shares become freely tradable as described in Section 2.2. No fractional shares will be issued; fractions will be rounded up to the nearest whole share. If freely tradable Conversion Shares are not delivered to the Holder by the Maturity Date, and such failure continues for ten (10) days thereafter (the “Grace Period”), the Company shall pay the Holder, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount in cash equal to two percent (2%) per month (prorated for any partial month) of the outstanding Conversion Amount, accruing from the end of the Grace Period until such shares are delivered, regardless of whether the delivery deadline in the first sentence of this Section 2.6 has passed, except to the extent delivery is prevented by the Exchange Cap or Section 2.5. 2.7 Fundamental Transactions. If the Company merges or consolidates, sells substantially all of its assets, or reclassifies its Common Stock before the Maturity Date, the Company may, at its option, either (a) prepay this Note under Section 1.4, or (b) cause the successor to assume this Note, in which case the Holder will receive on conversion the consideration a holder of the Conversion Shares would have received. 2.8 Reservation. The Company shall reserve a number of shares of Common Stock sufficient to effect conversion of this Note at the Floor Price, up to the Exchange Cap. Section 3. Registration Rights 3.1 Required Registration. The Company shall file with the SEC a registration statement (the “Registration Statement”) covering the resale of the Conversion Shares (the “Registrable Securities”) within ninety (90) days after the Issuance Date, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to have it declared effective as promptly as practicable and to keep it effective until the Registrable Securities have been sold or may be sold under Rule 144 without volume or manner-of-sale restrictions. 3.2 Piggyback Registration. If, before the ninetieth (90th) day after the Issuance Date, the Company files a registration statement for its own account or for others (other than on Form S-4 or S-8 or relating to an employee benefit plan or business combination), the Company shall give the Holder at least five (5) days’ prior written notice and include the Registrable Securities the Holder requests within three (3) days after notice, subject to customary underwriter cutbacks. Filing a registration statement that includes the Registrable Securities satisfies Section 3.1. 3.3 Expenses; Cooperation; Status. The Company bears registration expenses, other than the Holder’s selling commissions, transfer taxes and its own counsel fees. The Holder shall furnish information reasonably requested by the Company for the registration statement. The Company shall keep the Holder reasonably informed of the status of the Registration Statement, including by providing written updates at least every thirty (30) days and promptly upon its filing, receipt of any SEC comments and effectiveness. Except as set forth in Section 2.6, the Company’s failure to meet any registration deadline shall not be an Event of Default, and no liquidated damages shall apply. Page 4 Section 4. Events of Default 4.1 Events of Default. Each of the following is an “Event of Default”: (a) the Company fails to pay any amount when due and does not cure within ten (10) Business Days after written notice; (b) the Company fails to deliver Conversion Shares when required and does not cure within ten (10) Trading Days after written notice; (c) the Company materially breaches any other covenant in this Note and does not cure within thirty (30) days after written notice; or (d) the Company commences a voluntary bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding, or an involuntary proceeding against it is not dismissed within sixty (60) days. 4.2 Remedies. Upon an Event of Default that is continuing, the Holder may by written notice declare the outstanding Principal Amount and accrued interest immediately due and payable in cash (automatically, in the case of clause (d)). The Holder’s remedies are limited to those in this Note and applicable law; except as set forth in Section 2.6, no default premium, liquidated damages or buy-in payment applies. Section 5. Miscellaneous 5.1 Independent Counsel. The Holder has the right to retain, and has been advised to retain, its own independent legal, tax and financial counsel, at the Holder’s own expense, to review and negotiate this Note. The Holder acknowledges that Sichenzia Ross Ference Carmel LLP represents only the Company and has not represented or advised the Holder, and that the Holder has either consulted its own counsel or knowingly elected not to do so. This Note shall be deemed jointly drafted and not construed against either party. 5.2 Holder Representations. The Holder is an “accredited investor” under Rule 501(a) of Regulation D, is acquiring this Note for its own account for investment, and will not transfer this Note or the shares except in compliance with securities laws. 5.3 Transfer. This Note may not be assigned or transferred by the Holder without the Company’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except to an affiliate of the Holder that is an accredited investor. 5.4 Notices. Notices shall be in writing and are effective when delivered by email (if before 5:00 p.m. New York time on a Business Day, otherwise the next Business Day) or one (1) Business Day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, to the addresses on the signature page. 5.5 Governing Law; Venue; Jury Waiver. This Note is governed by New York law, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction. EACH PARTY WAIVES TRIAL BY JURY. Each party bears its own legal fees, except that the prevailing party in any action to enforce this Note may recover its reasonable attorneys’ fees. 5.6 Amendment; Entire Agreement. This Note may be amended or waived only in a writing signed by the Company and the Holder, and it constitutes the entire agreement of the parties on its subject matter. 5.7 Definitions. “Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which banks in New York, New York are closed. “Trading Day” means a day on which the Trading Market is open for trading. “Trading Market” means The Nasdaq Global Market, The Nasdaq Capital Market or such other national securities exchange on which the Common Stock is then listed. “VWAP” means the daily volume-weighted average price of the Common Stock on the Trading Market as reported by Bloomberg L.P. [Signature Page Follows] Page 5 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Company has executed this Note as of the Issuance Date. VENHUB GLOBAL, INC. I, a Cayman Islands exempted company (“ SPAC ”) and American Industrial Technologies, Inc., a Nevada corporation, formerly known as Q1 Holdings, Inc. (the “ Company ”). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this amendment to the LOI (this “ Amendment ”) shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the LOI. In consideration of the mutual promises and agreements contained in this Amendment, and for other good and valuable consideration, the sufficiency and adequacy of which is hereby acknowledged, the undersigned hereby agree as follows: 1. Amendment to Termination . The first sentence of Section 17 of the LOI entitled “Termination” is hereby amended by deleting it in its entirety and replacing it with the following: “This Letter can be terminated as follows: (a) by the mutual written agreement of the Parties to terminate this Letter; (b) by SPAC upon its determination that the due diligence review set forth in Section 6 has not been completed to its reasonable satisfaction; (c) by SPAC if the Company has not delivered the Company’s and Crosscall’s audited financial statements for the periods ending December 31, 2024 and 2025, the reviewed financial statements for the period ending June 30, 2026, and the reviewed financial statements for the period ending September 30, 2026, by December 23, 2026 or (d) by SPAC or the Company upon the expiration of the Exclusivity Period if no definitive agreement has been signed by such date.” 2. Miscellaneous . Except as expressly provided in this Amendment, all of the terms and provisions in the LOI are and shall remain in full force and effect, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein. This Amendment does not constitute, directly or by implication, an amendment, modification or waiver of any provision of the LOI, or any other right, remedy, power or privilege of any party to the LOI, except as expressly set forth herein. Any reference to the LOI in the LOI or any other agreement, document, instrument or certificate entered into or issued in connection therewith shall hereinafter mean the LOI, as amended or modified by this Amendment (or as the LOI may be further amended or modified after the date hereof in accordance with the terms thereof). This Amendment may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall be deemed to be one and the same agreement. A signed copy of this Amendment delivered by facsimile, email, or other means of electronic transmission (including in portable document format (.pdf)) shall be deemed to have the same legal effect as delivery of an original signed copy of this Amendment. The terms of this Amendment shall be interpreted, enforced, governed by and construed in a manner consistent with the provisions of the LOI. [Signature Page Follows] Please acknowledge your acceptance of and agreement to the foregoing by signing and returning a counterpart of this Amendment to the undersigned as soon as possible. Sincerely, SIM ACQUISITION CORP.
